title: Count marbles, not colours
skill: Probability of picking a colour (or not a colour) from a bag of marbles of different counts.

knowledge: fractions as part of a whole

concept: Each marble (or ball) is equally likely to be picked, not each colour. So count marbles, not colours.
Probability = (marbles that fit) ÷ (ALL the marbles). It is a number from 0 to 1, never more than 1.
explanation.visualNote: Reuses the family's own colour table figure.

workedExamples.prompt: A bag has 6 red and 8 blue marbles, as in the table. Meena picks one marble without looking. What is the probability that it is red? (A fraction is fine.)
lines: All the marbles: 6 red + 8 blue = 14, each equally likely

alternativeExplanation.title: Scale from 0 to 1
text: No matching marbles: 0. All of them: 1. Some: in between; more matching marbles means nearer 1.

alternativeMethods.name: Number every marble
example: number the marbles 1, 2, 3, …; each number is equally likely

whatWentWrong: In "A bag has 4 red, 2 blue and 4 green marbles, as in the table. Farhan picks one marble without looking. What is the probability that it is red? (A fraction is fine.)", one wrong answer is 1/3.
Each colour was taken as equally likely (1 out of 3 colours). The colours have different numbers of marbles, so count marbles, not colours.
Colours with more marbles are more likely: count marbles, not colours.
screens.counterCheck: Check: there are 4 red but only 2 blue, so blue is LESS likely than red. So the colours do not all have the same chance.
solvedCorrectly: All the marbles: 4 red + 2 blue + 4 green = 10, each equally likely
